**Convert a folder you already have into a drive, without copying it.** A
folder full of large files becomes a drive in minutes rather than hours, and
needs almost no free space. Drives can be turned back into plain folders the
same way.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.4.0-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.4.0-macos-arm64.dmg` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings are kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** open the disk image and drag **Cloak** onto **Applications**. The
app isn't notarized, so before opening it the first time, clear the download
quarantine: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cloak.app` (or
right-click Cloak → Open, then Open again). macFUSE's kernel extension must be
allowed; on Apple Silicon that means its one-time Reduced Security setup.

## New

- **Convert folder.** Pick a folder, a name and a password, and cloak first
  checks the folder and shows what it will do: how many files, how long it
  should take, and anything in the way (names a drive can't hold, links,
  read-only or cloud-only files). Nothing is changed until you press
  Convert. Each file is renamed and has its first and last 64 KB encrypted
  where it lies, so a 40 GB video takes no longer than a photo. System clutter
  (`.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`) is deleted.
- **Safe to interrupt.** If converting stops (a crash, a power cut, a closed
  laptop), the drive's card says so and offers **Resume**, which carries on
  where it stopped with the same password. The drive can't be unlocked until
  it's finished.
- **Turn a drive back into a plain folder** with the new button on a locked
  drive's card. It's just as quick, and just as safe to interrupt.

Converting changes your files where they are, so keep a backup of anything
irreplaceable until you've checked the drive. If the folder is synced
(OneDrive, Dropbox…), the service may keep the unconverted originals in its
version history; the check warns about this.

## Fixed

- **macOS:** the mount no longer uses more memory the longer a drive stays
  unlocked. Browsing big folders, Spotlight and backups used to grow it
  steadily until the drive was locked.

## Known limitations

- Converting and turning back haven't been tried on a real Mac yet (they're
  tested on Windows, and the engine's tests pass on macOS and Linux).
- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
